To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HBIM model can be a useful tool to support the planned conservation approach; HBIM process is not an automatic process; HBIM model can integrate historical sources, geometrical survey data and conservation data.
HBIM can be useful to increase the efficiency of planned conservation.

HBIM is a powerful tool for the management of cultural heritage assets; HBIM is not a fully automatized process, it requires a deep understanding of historical sources; HBIM can be an integrated archive of all information related to a cultural heritage asset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we interpret the data?
a practical application of HBIM to cultural heritage items, and in particular to a complex building, such as a church.
the development of a coherent and useful HBIM model for the management of cultural heritage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HBIM is a useful tool for planned conservation.
HBIM is an appropriate tool for planned conservation, but it is not an automatic process.
HBIM can support the planned conservation process, but the HBIM process itself requires the support of a comprehensive and detailed knowledge of the building.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HBIM process requires a deep understanding of building and of historical sources, and it is a way to increase the effectiveness of the planned conservation.
HBIM is not a mere 3D model, it is an instrument for data integration, for interpretation and understanding of the building and for its future management.
HBIM, as a useful tool to support planned conservation, needs a deep knowledge of historical sources and a deep understanding for the building, in its historical and architectural aspects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HBIM is a process that requires a deep knowledge of the building, both from geometrical and from historical point of view.
the HBIM model is a useful tool for planned conservation.
a HBIM model, in order to be coherent with reality, requires a deep knowledge and interpretation of the building and its history.
